tags.gist: Answers Q10 with a measurement-system qualification package, likened to the performance specifications clinical laboratories must establish before reporting.
Says acceptance criteria for open-ended outputs cannot be read unless the evaluation process's own variability is known, which bears on PCCPs.
Summarizes ten recommendations: qualification components, a null comparison, validated observation windows, separate escalation outcomes, mapped re-benchmarking and adjudicator bridging.
Reports that specifying benchmark content and scoring was not enough, on its own, to make the numbers interpretable.
Calls the ten benchmarking elements a sound content specification, with the safety elements naming the failure modes that matter.
Says the paper is right to ask about construct validity alongside sponsor benchmarks, independence and optimisation to the test.
Says construct validity needs evidence about how the scoring instrument behaves, as laboratories establish performance specifications, not just its contents.
Reports that scoring window, reference labels and implementation each shifted results independently, so unqualified scores have uncharacterised precision.
Wants sponsors to characterise device, adjudicator and reference-standard variability together, since PCCP acceptance criteria for generated language depend on it.
Warns an uncalibrated threshold either passes evaluation noise as change or, set high, blocks most modifications and returns them to FDA.
Would have sponsors qualify the measurement system through six evidence components before any device result is read.
Wants reference answers fixed in advance and independently of the adjudicator, or scores measure agreement rather than correctness.
Wants multi-turn sponsors to show the scoring window is long enough to capture the behaviour measured.
Wants automated adjudicators calibrated against qualified human raters dimension by dimension, since aggregates hide weak dimensions.
Wants evidence that the configuration evaluated matched the configuration specified, since declared and executed settings diverge.
Wants a written rule for resolving rater or adjudicator disagreement before any result is seen.
Wants adjudicator, corpus, prompt versions and a configuration hash recorded with every reported score.
Urges a low-burden null comparison: resample the unchanged configuration against itself to build an empirical null before claiming change.
Calls the two-stage structure of benchmarking then clinical confirmation correct.
Offers an openly licensed benchmark with independent ground truth and provenance manifest as a reproducible starting point, not a finished standard.
Says multi-turn scores collapse required-action turn, timeliness and observation window, so a late escalation and a miss can score alike.
Says a late escalation remains a timeliness failure whatever follows; recovery should be recorded, not credited.
Asks that the observation window be prespecified, justified and validated, with timeliness and later recovery reported separately.
Agrees the two escalation errors are incommensurable and says they need separate denominators and thresholds, never only a composite.
Wants missed and unnecessary escalations reported as separate prespecified outcomes with separate denominators, requiring declared non-escalation cases in corpora.
Accepts context-specific composite weighting if component rates stay reported and weights are justified prospectively by consequence.
Proposes scaling re-benchmarking by a published mapping from seven modification types to affected competency suites, with partial scope justified.
Wants a fixed critical-safety regression core re-run unchanged on every modification that could alter outputs, controls or actions.
Says change-triggered re-benchmarking should complement periodic assessment, which catches undeclared drift in models, dependencies or use environment.
Wants the adjudicator pinned and versioned in the baseline, with any adjudicator change bridge-tested before comparison to history.
Finds the two-axis framing a sensible way to choose among confirmation approaches and sees no need for a third axis.
Says a lighter confirmation approach justified by benchmark strength should require qualification evidence, with well-qualified benchmarks carrying more weight.
Says synthetic conversations suit stress tests of rare, adversarial and safety-critical situations and controlled ablations, though not real use.
Says clinician validation of a synthetic case confirms coherence and label, not that the case distribution matches use.
Opposes naive pooling; combination needs a common estimand, distribution comparison, prospective weighting and sensitivity analysis, else report separately.
Wants reference labels established apart from the generating model and adversarial cases built against a declared failure taxonomy.
Prefers open, reproducible methods with independence concentrated on reference-standard adjudication and third-party sequestered safety sets over certification.
Says paid certification by few bodies raises cost and concentration; targeted independence with open methods gives most assurance.
Describes planned research reporting minimum detectable effect against repeated runs, so sponsors and reviewers can read off needed repeats.
Recommends requiring six-component qualification evidence on the measurement system behind any benchmark gating device evaluation.
Recommends considering a required null comparison of the unchanged configuration against itself as minimum evidence of discrimination.
Recommends treating the multi-turn observation window as a validated parameter and reporting timeliness apart from recovery.
Recommends separate prespecified outcomes and denominators for under- and over-escalation, with declared non-escalation cases.
Recommends mapped re-benchmarking by modification type, an invariant safety core, and periodic assessment kept alongside change triggers.
Recommends that swapping the adjudicator count as an evaluation-system change needing bridge testing.
Recommends not pooling benchmarking and confirmation evidence unless stated conditions are met.
Recommends synthetic case labels be set or verified independently of the generating model.
Recommends open methods, reproducible sponsor testing and targeted independent adjudication rather than a certification regime.
Recommends every acceptance criterion come with a characterisation of evaluation variability, treating one without as hard to interpret.
